subject: Legal review: Benchmark report claims + disclaimers (v0.9 copy + landing page)
body:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwoodinference.com>, Sofia Mendes <sofia.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>, Ethan Wallace <ethan.wallace@redwoodinference.com>, Henry Cho <henry.cho@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Jun 12, 2025 at 9:14 AM
Subject: Legal review: Benchmark report claims + disclaimers (v0.9 copy + landing page)

Michael, Sofia — looping you in for legal review of our benchmark report copy + landing page claims. We’re aiming to lock publishable language by next week to stay on schedule.

Request:
1) Confirm what comparative statements are allowable (esp. “best / leading / #1”, competitor references, and “latency/$” framing).
2) Confirm required disclaimer language placement (PDF + landing page + interactive table tooltips).
3) Identify any claims that require additional substantiation or should be removed.

Materials (Drive links + attachment stubs):
- Report copy (v0.9): Redwood_Benchmark_Report_v0.9_COPY.docx
- Landing page copy (v1.2): LandingPage_Copy_v1.2.txt
- Methodology summary (v0.6): Methodology_Summary_v0.6.docx

We are planning to publish:
- Interactive web table (model x region + filters)
- Downloadable PDF
- Blog post summarizing key takeaways

Known sensitive areas:
- “Latency per dollar” metric is new to many readers; we have a methodology section but want to ensure it’s legally safe.
- We may include competitor context in a small “industry baseline” callout (no vendor logos; likely anonymized or caveated).

If helpful, we can jump on a 20-min working session today or tomorrow.

Thanks,
Soojin
Soojin Lee
Director of Product Marketing | Redwood Inference


---

From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwoodinference.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sofia Mendes <sofia.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>, Ethan Wallace <ethan.wallace@redwoodinference.com>, Henry Cho <henry.cho@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Jun 12, 2025 at 11:02 AM
Subject: Re: Legal review: Benchmark report claims + disclaimers (v0.9 copy + landing page)

Thanks. Reviewed the attached copy and skimmed methodology summary.

High-level guidance (not final approval; see tracked edits requests below):

A) Comparative / superlative claims
- Avoid “best,” “#1,” “industry-leading,” “beats everyone,” “most efficient,” and similar unqualified superlatives.
- If you compare, you must: (i) name the comparator, (ii) identify material assumptions, (iii) provide substantiation and retention of source data, and (iv) avoid implying universality.
- “Faster and cheaper” is risky unless tightly scoped to a specific model, region, context length, and workload definition.

B) “Latency/$” metric framing
- Okay to use as a defined metric, but only if the definition is immediately adjacent or linked and not buried.
- Avoid implying it is an industry standard. Recommend “our latency-per-dollar metric” / “latency per dollar (as defined in this report).”

C) Competitor context
- The anonymized “industry baseline” callout is still a comparative claim. We would need to ensure it is not misleading and that we can defend it.
- Strong recommendation: for v1, omit competitor baselines entirely from the public PDF/landing page. You can include a qualitative “why latency/$ matters” without competitor numbers.

D) Disclaimers (must be visible where claims appear)
- Include “Results vary by workload, model version, region, and configuration.”
- Include “Benchmarks run on Redwood Inference platform under defined settings; see methodology.”
- If any results are not generally available (e.g., unreleased model versions or limited regions), state this clearly.

Specific copy changes requested (please apply and resend for approval):
1) Landing page hero: “The most cost-efficient LLM inference across regions.” → change to “Benchmarking production inference economics across regions.”
2) Section header: “Redwood delivers the best latency/$.” → remove “best.” Suggest “Redwood optimizes latency per dollar.”
3) PDF Exec summary: “2–4x better latency/$ than other providers” → remove. If you want a multiplier, it must be tied to named competitors and fully scoped. Otherwise, avoid.
4) Anywhere you say “guarantee” re: latency or cost → change to “designed to” / “targeting” unless it’s an SLA term (and then coordinate with Contracts).

Approval conditions (for publishable version):
- Methodology link included on landing page above the fold.
- A short disclaimer placed directly under any headline metric chart.
- Data retention confirmation (raw logs/manifests + derived datasets) per internal policy.

Sofia will send line edits re: phrasing/caveats.

Michael Grant
Associate General Counsel | Redwood Inference


---

From: Sofia Mendes <sofia.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwoodinference.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>, Ethan Wallace <ethan.wallace@redwoodinference.com>, Henry Cho <henry.cho@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Jun 12, 2025 at 12:26 PM
Subject: Re: Legal review: Benchmark report claims + disclaimers (v0.9 copy + landing page)

Adding specifics and proposed disclaimer language.

1) Proposed standard disclaimer block (web + PDF)
Use verbatim where possible:
“Benchmark results are provided for informational purposes only and reflect performance under the workload definitions and configurations described in the Methodology. Results may vary based on prompts, model versions, traffic patterns, regions, hardware availability, and system configuration. This report does not constitute a guarantee of performance.”

2) “Real-world” / “production” phrasing
- “Production” is okay if you clarify it refers to the workload mix/prompt set we selected, not a claim that it matches every customer.
- Please avoid “representative of all production workloads.” Prefer: “designed to reflect common production patterns.”

3) Charts and captions
- Any chart that implies ranking needs a caption specifying: (i) date range of runs, (ii) regions included, (iii) the models/versions used, (iv) whether caching/batching was enabled/disabled.
- For the interactive table: a persistent “About this data” drawer is strongly preferred over a single footnote.

4) Suggested copy edits (tracked changes requested)
- Replace “consistent across regions” with “measured across multiple regions” unless you have statistical thresholds defined (e.g., variance bands). “Consistent” can imply guarantee.
- Replace “apples-to-apples” with “controlled configuration” / “standardized harness.”
- Avoid “unbiased.” Prefer “pre-registered methodology” / “reproducible harness.”

5) Competitor callouts
Agree with Michael: remove competitor numbers/logos for v1.
If Marketing insists on competitor mention, you must include: competitor name(s), exact configuration parity statement, and access constraints (which is hard to do cleanly).

If you apply these changes today, we can do a quick final pass tomorrow.

Sofia Mendes
Senior Counsel (Commercial & Product) | Redwood Inference


---

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwoodinference.com>, Sofia Mendes <sofia.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>, Ethan Wallace <ethan.wallace@redwoodinference.com>, Henry Cho <henry.cho@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Jun 12, 2025 at 3:47 PM
Subject: Re: Legal review: Benchmark report claims + disclaimers (v0.9 copy + landing page)

This is helpful — thank you both.

Actions we’ll take for v1 (confirming alignment):
- Remove competitor baselines entirely from public-facing PDF + landing page.
- Replace superlatives (“best,” “most cost-efficient,” “2–4x better”) with scoped, descriptive language.
- Add methodology link above the fold + “About this data” drawer in the interactive table.
- Add standard disclaimer block (Sofia’s language) under hero chart and in PDF footer.

Two items to confirm:
1) “Latency per dollar” naming: Are we okay to title the interactive page “Latency per dollar benchmark” if we immediately define it in the subhead (“as defined in this report”)? Alternative we can use: “Inference economics benchmark (latency vs cost).”
2) “Regional consistency” claim: Engineering wants to say “predictable across regions.” We can soften to “comparable measurement across regions” as you suggested, but want to ensure we don’t undercut the story.

Naomi (Security) added on CC re: the data retention/access controls item. We can confirm retention of run manifests + redaction process if needed.

We’ll incorporate edits tonight and send updated copy + highlighted diffs.

Soojin


---

From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwoodinference.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sofia Mendes <sofia.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>, Ethan Wallace <ethan.wallace@redwoodinference.com>, Henry Cho <henry.cho@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Jun 13, 2025 at 10:19 AM
Subject: Re: Legal review: Benchmark report claims + disclaimers (v0.9 copy + landing page)

1) Title
“Latency per dollar benchmark” is acceptable if the subtitle includes “(as defined in this report)” and there is a clear definition in the first screenful (not behind a click).
Approved example:
Title: “Latency per dollar benchmark”
Subtitle: “A reproducible inference economics benchmark (latency per dollar as defined in this report).”

2) Regional language
Avoid “predictable” unless you’re referencing a contractual SLA or a statistically-defined threshold.
Acceptable:
- “Measured across multiple regions”
- “Comparable performance measured across regions under a standardized harness”
- “Regional results included for transparency; see methodology”

On retention: Naomi, please confirm in writing that the raw logs/manifests are retained per policy and that public artifacts are redacted. That’s a condition for us.

Once you send the updated copy with diffs, Sofia and I can provide final sign-off or any remaining edits.

Michael


---

From: Sofia Mendes <sofia.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwoodinference.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>, Ethan Wallace <ethan.wallace@redwoodinference.com>, Henry Cho <henry.cho@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Jun 13, 2025 at 4:48 PM
Subject: Re: Legal review: Benchmark report claims + disclaimers (v0.9 copy + landing page)

Reviewed the updated landing page text (Drive link you sent this afternoon) and the revised PDF exec summary language.

Status: Approved with conditions below.

Approved changes observed:
- Removed competitor references and multiplier claims.
- Hero language now descriptive vs. superlative.
- Methodology is linked above the fold.
- Disclaimer block is present under the primary chart and in the PDF.

Remaining required conditions (must be implemented before publish):
1) Add an explicit “Not a guarantee” sentence adjacent to the interactive table (not only in the drawer). It can be a one-liner under the filters.
2) Add a “Data freshness” note (run window date range) on the landing page and PDF front matter.
3) Add a note that results can vary with caching/batching settings and link to the exact settings used.

Nice-to-have (non-blocking, but recommended):
- Replace “apples-to-apples” in the blog draft with “standardized harness.”

If the above three required conditions are met and you do not add new comparative language, Legal considers the claims/disclaimers package approved for launch.

Sofia Mendes
Senior Counsel (Commercial & Product) | Redwood Inference
